assessments.scope: Typed rejection by parse/parseAsync of an unresolved Recur that is present only in the schema's input type (or only in its output type), rather than in both.
assessments.reason: The related type tests added for this patch (parse.test-d.ts / parseAsync.test-d.ts) only exercise `parse(array(Recur), [])` / `parseAsync(array(Recur), [])`, where the placeholder is present in both the input and the output type, so they do not discriminate the input-side check the public issue hint requires. No supplied test uses a schema whose transform leaves Recur only in one inferred type.

assessments.scope: Recur placeholder shape and its runtime failure when used unresolved.
assessments.reason: recur.test.ts asserts the placeholder schema shape and that Recur['~run'] adds an issue mentioning Recur; this matches the public contract for the placeholder's runtime behavior.

assessments.scope: Sync resolution of Recur through array, record, map, set, pipe and intersect, including identity of resolved positions and non-mutation of schemas without Recur.
assessments.reason: recursive.test.ts checks resolved self-reference identity and parse/safeParse for array, record, map, set, pipe and intersect, and verifies unrelated schemas are not cloned; these cover the contract's listed sync composition positions.

assessments.scope: Async resolution of Recur through arrayAsync, recordAsync, mapAsync, setAsync, pipeAsync and intersectAsync, including acceptance of sync subschemas.
assessments.reason: recursiveAsync.test.ts mirrors the sync coverage with parseAsync/safeParseAsync calls, resolved-position identity and the sync-schema acceptance case, matching the async contract.

assessments.scope: Typed rejection by safeParse/safeParseAsync of an unresolved Recur present in only one of the schema's input or output types.
assessments.reason: The related safeParse.test-d.ts / safeParseAsync.test-d.ts rejection tests only call `safeParse(array(Recur), [])` / `safeParseAsync(array(Recur), [])`, where the placeholder is in both inferred types; no supplied test exercises a schema where a transform leaves Recur only in input or only in output, so the single-sided check is not observed.

assessments.scope: Whether the record `__proto__` host test observes any recursive-composition contract.
assessments.reason: The seed exercises record's `__proto__` handling only; its link to the changed recursive declarations is a lexical `parse` name coincidence, and the recursive contract is not exercised here.

assessments.scope: Whether the getDotPath host test observes any recursive-composition contract.
assessments.reason: The seed builds issue paths for getDotPath and is linked only by an unresolved `get` name token; it does not exercise Recur, recursive or the parse-family rejection.

goals.existing_validation: parse.test-d.ts 'parse with unresolved Recur' asserts `// @ts-expect-error parse(array(Recur), [])` and that a `recursive(...)`-wrapped schema infers `InferOutput`.
goals.missing_relation: Rejection when Recur is present only in the schema's input type (the transform removes it from the output type), which is the case that separates an input-side check from an output-only check.
goals.preconditions: A legal schema whose inferred input type is the Recur marker but whose output type is a plain value, e.g. `const schema = pipe(Recur, transform(() => 42));`, passed to `parse(schema, 'x')`.
goals.object_binding: `parse`'s first argument (schema parameter, position 0) carrying the unresolved Recur in its input type.
goals.observation: The call must be rejected at compile time while no unrelated type error is introduced in that expression.
goals.expectation: parse rejects the schema because `RejectUnresolvedRecur` detects the placeholder in the schema's input type even though the output type is `number`.
goals.oracle_basis: Public issue: typed parse/safeParse/parseAsync/safeParseAsync should reject unresolved Recur, and its hint that the placeholder may appear in only one of the input or output types ('checking only one can miss cases').

goals.existing_validation: safeParse.test-d.ts 'safeParse with unresolved Recur' asserts `// @ts-expect-error safeParse(array(Recur), [])` and a resolved-recur inference case.
goals.missing_relation: Rejection when Recur is present only in the schema's output type (the input type is free of the placeholder), which separates an output-side check from an input-only check.
goals.preconditions: A legal schema whose input type is a plain value and whose output type is the Recur placeholder schema, e.g. `const schema = pipe(string(), transform(() => Recur));`, passed to `safeParse(schema, 'x')`.
goals.object_binding: `safeParse`'s first argument (schema parameter, position 0) whose output type still contains the Recur placeholder.
goals.observation: The call must be rejected at compile time, with no unrelated type error in that expression.
goals.expectation: safeParse rejects the schema because `RejectUnresolvedRecur` detects the placeholder in the schema's output type even though the input type is `string`.
goals.oracle_basis: Public issue: typed safeParse/safeParseAsync should reject unresolved Recur, and its hint that the placeholder must be checked in both input and output because it may appear in only one.
